title: ITC and IMS actions
learn: What accept, reject and pending in IMS do to 2B
Why a bill misses 2B, and when its credit comes
Which 3B row reverses blocked and unpaid-bill credit
do: Decide 11 records: the IMS action and February’s credit

documents.title: Our IMS rules · GST team memo
documents.subject: IMS and input credit: how we work
body: For every client whose returns we prepare. Read it before you act in IMS.
## Matching
- Match the books with 2B on GSTIN, invoice number and amount, never on the supplier’s name alone.
## Acting in IMS
- Accept a record that is the client’s and correct, whether or not the client has booked it yet. A genuine bill whose credit is blocked is accepted too; its credit comes out in 3B Table 4B(1).
- Keep pending a record that is the client’s but cannot be claimed this month, such as goods that reach after the month ends. Accept it in the month they arrive.
- Reject only a record that is not the client’s: nothing ordered and nothing received. Add a remark.
- Act on every record. No action counts as accepted when 2B is made.
- After any change, recompute 2B before the 3B is filed.
## Not in IMS
- Nothing to act on there. Find out why: the supplier has not filed, has filed it on another GSTIN, or its GSTIN is cancelled. No credit until the record reaches the client’s 2B.
- Filed on another GSTIN: that GSTIN rejects it in its own IMS, and the supplier corrects the buyer’s GSTIN in its next GSTR-1. GSTR-1A cannot change a buyer’s GSTIN.
## Unpaid bills
- A bill still unpaid 180 days after its date: reverse the credit in 3B Table 4B(2), with any interest payable under section 50, and take it back when the client pays.

tasks.title: Decide the 11 records
tasks.prompt: Varun’s sheet lists the 11 records his match could not settle. Open each with its papers; our IMS rules, the register, the IMS print, 2B and the rest are under Other papers. For each, pick February’s 3B treatment, the IMS action and, if it isn’t claimed, the reason. Your calls go to Neethu when you move on.

lockOnLeave.note: You can’t change them after this.
lockOnLeave.done: Handed to Neethu. You can read your calls but not change them.

hints: Start from the record’s line. In books only: why did it miss 2B? Read the return status and Varun’s papers. In 2B only: whose bill is it, when did the goods come, when was it booked? In both: the same bill? Unpaid: how many days?
Then ask if the law lets Tamhini keep the credit: what was the bill for, and is it still unpaid 180 days after its date? Our IMS rules give the action either way.

options.label: Supplier reported it on another GSTIN

fields.label: Your note for the file
fields.placeholder: For example: GSTIN, number and amount agree with 2B

items.label: Alandi Paper Products
items.note: Alandi: its GSTIN has been cancelled since 15 September, so nothing it bills reaches 2B. Nothing to act on in IMS, and no credit while it stays cancelled. Tamhini pays Alandi the bill value without the GST, as it has since October.

items.label: Hebbal Tooling Solutions
items.note: Hebbal: in 2B, but delivery is at Chakan, and the inserts and hobs reached the tool crib on 4 March. No goods in February, no February credit. Keep it pending, as our rules say, and accept it in March. Pallavi’s idea is a month early.

items.label: Kolak Polypack
items.note: Kolak again. January’s bill, held back then because it missed January’s 2B. Kolak added it by GSTR-1A on 15 February, after the cut-off, so it sits in February’s 2B. Accept and claim it now.

items.label: Palar Seals and Gaskets
items.note: Palar: a debit note bringing the seal rate up to the PO’s ₹29.00. Rohit checked it, but it never left the purchase desk. It is Tamhini’s and right, so accept and claim it, and ask Pallavi to book it in February.

items.label: Phillaur Fasteners
items.note: Phillaur did file, on 11 March, but put 2281 on Hosur’s GSTIN; Varun found it in Hosur’s IMS. It is not in Chakan’s IMS or 2B, so no credit this month. Varun rejects it at Hosur, and Phillaur corrects it in its March GSTR-1.

items.label: Rankala Forgings
items.note: Rankala: one bill. Pallavi typed 2214; the portal has RF/2214/26-27. GSTIN, date and tax agree to the rupee, so accept and claim, and ask Pallavi to enter the full number in the books.

items.label: Ravet Car Care
items.note: Ravet: servicing of the MD’s sedan. Repairs of a passenger car, 13 seats or fewer, are blocked under section 17(5). The bill is genuine, so accept it, don’t reject it; its ₹6,840 comes into 4A(5) from 2B and goes out in 4B(1).

items.label: Sakhare Surface Treatment
items.note: Sakhare: the bill and 2B say ₹4,864.50 each of CGST and SGST; Pallavi rounded it to ₹4,865. Fifty paise is a round-off, not a mismatch. Accept and claim, at 2B’s figure.

items.label: Sawangi Pressed Metals
items.note: Sawangi: Rohit has never bought from them. No PO, no GRN, no vendor code. It isn’t Tamhini’s, so reject it with a remark. Left on No action, the portal would have counted it as accepted.

items.label: Shirur Metrology Labs
items.note: Shirur: the calibration is done and booked, but Shirur hasn’t filed February’s GSTR-1, so the bill is in neither IMS nor 2B. No credit yet. Pallavi chases Shirur; the credit comes in the 2B after it files.

items.label: Mundhwa Lubricants and Chemicals
items.note: Mundhwa: bill of 4 August, credit taken in August, unpaid while the oil dispute runs. The 180 days ran out on 31 January, so February’s 3B reverses ₹15,480 each of CGST and SGST in 4B(2). It comes back when Tamhini pays.

tasks.title: Work out February’s credit table
tasks.prompt: Now Table 4 of February’s 3B, from your IMS calls. Start from 2B as generated on 14 March and take out what you kept pending or rejected: that is the recomputed 2B, which fills 4A(5). Then the two reversals and the net. Enter positive figures.
hints: Pending and rejected records drop out when 2B is recomputed; the rest of 2B fills 4A(5). The blocked bill and the 180-day bill then come out in 4B.

cells.line: ITC available in GSTR-2B as generated on 14 March (every record on No action)
Less: records kept pending or rejected in IMS

notes.r2.ig: Hebbal’s ₹57,600 leaves 2B when you recompute, and reaches March’s 2B when you accept it then. Accepted now, it would be March’s credit taken in February.
notes.r2.cg: Sawangi’s bill moves to the rejected part of 2B and gives no credit at all.
notes.r3.ig: 4A(5) is the recomputed 2B. Kolak’s January bill and Palar’s debit note are in it; Phillaur’s and Shirur’s bills are not.
notes.r4.cg: Ravet’s tax came in through 2B with the accepted bill, so it goes out here, for good.
notes.r5.cg: Mundhwa’s August credit goes out now and comes back in 4A(5) the month Tamhini pays.
notes.r6.cg: 4C is what reaches the credit ledger for February.

tasks.title: Draft the supplier mail
tasks.prompt: Phillaur’s bill 2281 needs a correction only Phillaur can make. Draft the mail Pallavi will send them: pick the right line for each part.
hints: Phillaur did file, on time. Read what our IMS rules say about a record filed on another GSTIN, and remember the credit follows 2B.

options.text: Your invoice PF/2026-27/2281 of 18 February (₹2,10,000 + IGST ₹37,800) is made out to our Chakan GSTIN, 27ZHDCT5940H1Z4, but your February GSTR-1 reports it against our Hosur GSTIN, 33ZHDCT5940H1ZB.
options.why: Naming both GSTINs lets their accountant find the record at once. The paper is right; only the return entry went astray.

options.text: Your invoice PF/2026-27/2281 of 18 February (₹2,10,000 + IGST ₹37,800) is not in our GSTR-2B, because your February GSTR-1 has not been filed yet. Please file it at the earliest.
options.why: They filed on 11 March. The bill is sitting in Hosur’s IMS, not missing.

options.text: Your invoice PF/2026-27/2281 of 18 February (₹2,10,000 + IGST ₹37,800) carries a wrong GSTIN on its face, so it is not a valid tax invoice in our hands as it stands.
options.why: Read the bill again: it shows Chakan’s GSTIN. Only Phillaur’s GSTR-1 entry is wrong.

options.text: Please amend this record to our Chakan GSTIN through your GSTR-1A for February, before you file your February 3B, so that the credit reaches us this month.
options.why: GSTR-1A can’t change a buyer’s GSTIN; only a later GSTR-1 can. Even a GSTR-1A record reaches the buyer in the next month’s 2B, not this one.

options.text: Please amend this record to our Chakan GSTIN in your March GSTR-1, due on 11 April. Our Hosur unit is rejecting it in its IMS meanwhile.
options.why: Hosur’s rejection keeps the credit out of Hosur’s 3B, and the March GSTR-1 moves the bill to Chakan’s GSTIN.

options.text: Please take no action at your end: our Hosur unit will take the credit, as its 2B shows the invoice, and settle it with our Chakan unit.
options.why: Hosur never received the circlips, so the credit is not Hosur’s. Varun is rejecting it there.

options.text: We are taking the credit in our February return now, as the invoice is made out to Chakan; the amendment can follow when convenient.
options.why: Not before Chakan’s 2B shows it. Credit follows 2B, whatever the paper says.

options.text: We will take the credit in the month the amended record reaches our Chakan GSTR-2B. Please confirm once you have filed the amendment.
options.why: Filed by 11 April, the corrected record lands in March’s 2B, so the credit is claimed in March’s 3B.

options.text: We have lost the credit on this invoice, as our February return closes this week, and will deduct the GST from your next payment.
options.why: Nothing is lost: the credit comes in the month the amended record reaches Chakan’s 2B.

freeText.label: Your own line for the mail

wrap.text: Eleven records: four claimed now, five wait or never come, and two go out through 4B. I’ll tie your Table 4 to the recomputed 2B before Friday’s 3B. Pass the Phillaur mail to Pallavi today, and tell Varun to reject 2281 at Hosur.

wrapPartial.text: Before Friday, ask of each record you missed: whose is it, has it arrived, is the credit allowed, is it in Chakan’s 2B? That settles the IMS action and the 3B row. 4A(5) is 2B less what IMS held back. Nothing goes to Phillaur until every mail line is right.

wrapRetry.text: Work from each record’s own papers, not from 2B. Whose bill is it, did the goods come in February, is the credit allowed, and did the supplier file it on Chakan’s GSTIN? Then our IMS rules give the action and the Table 4 row.

passNeeds.note: Hebbal and Mundhwa count twice. You need 70% of the record marks to pass; a wrong 3B call scores nothing.

model.intro: Four of the eleven only needed a closer look and are claimed in February: Kolak, Palar, Rankala and Sakhare. Five stay out, for the reasons in the table. Ravet’s car service comes in through 2B and goes out in 4B(1); Mundhwa’s August credit goes out in 4B(2).

Pending now; accept in March’s IMS
Varun rejects at Hosur; Phillaur corrects it in its March GSTR-1; claimed in March
Pallavi chases Shirur; claimed in the month its bill reaches 2B

rows.w: Servicing of the MD’s sedan: blocked

rows.n: Out in 4B(2); back in 4A(5) when paid

blocks.text: Every difference between the books and the 2B of 14 March has a name:
2B is what suppliers uploaded, not what Tamhini may claim. IMS decides what stays in 2B’s ITC available; Table 4B then takes out what the law blocks or holds back.

principles: Reject only what isn’t the client’s; a genuine bill with blocked credit is accepted and reversed in 4B(1).
A credit that is only late comes in the month its fix lands: the supplier files or corrects the GSTIN, or the goods arrive.
4B(1) is credit gone for good; 4B(2) is credit that comes back, such as the credit on a bill unpaid for 180 days.

interview.q: What is IMS, and what can you do in it?
interview.checking: Whether you know how IMS actions shape the credit in GSTR-2B, and when each action fits.
outline: The GST portal’s Invoice Management System: I accept, reject or keep pending each bill a supplier uploads.
No action counts as accepted when 2B is made; pending and rejected bills don’t flow into the 3B.
Reject only what isn’t yours[[; in the simulation I rejected a stranger’s bill{rej|} and held one awaiting goods{pend|}]].

interview.q: A supplier’s bill for servicing the MD’s car shows in GSTR-2B. Do you reject it in IMS?
interview.checking: Whether you can tell a bill to reject from a credit to reverse, and where that credit goes.
outline: No. The bill is genuine and the client’s; blocked credit is no reason to reject it.
Its credit is blocked under section 17(5): accept the bill, then reverse the credit in 4B(1).
In the simulation a car-service bill went that way; one unpaid for 180 days went to 4B(2).
